structured_output.differences: The author's c1-c3 map directly onto the three conditions I derived in step 1 (owner membership, exact member count of 5, creation before March 2026); there is no material difference in scope or wording. The author's list doesn't separately flag the member-count ambiguity (bot-inclusive vs. bot-exclusive), but that's an interpretive nuance rather than a missing condition.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Slack distinguishes a 'Primary Owner' from other users who could hold an 'Owner' role, so the phrase is ambiguous in the abstract. But in this workspace only one user (U_VICTOR) has role 'owner' in user_teams, with no separate primary-owner flag, so both readings pick the same person and no candidate's status changes.

channel_members rows include the requesting bot (U01AGENBOT9) as a member of every channel. Whether 'members' means the total row count (including the bot) or only human members determines whether C_ATLAS (5 total / 4 human) or C_SIX (6 total / 5 human) is the match – the two readings select different channels.

Interpreting the cutoff in workspace-local time vs. UTC could matter for a channel created right at the March 1 boundary, but no channel's created_at falls close enough to that boundary (nearest are Feb 15 and Mar 4) for a timezone shift of a few hours to change any outcome.

structured_output.naturalness_note: Chaining three precise technical qualifiers - owner membership, an exact member count, and a specific creation-date cutoff - to identify one channel reads more like a constructed filter for a test than something a person would naturally type into Slack; a real user would more likely just name the channel.
